title: Graph
text: A Graph is an in-memory collection of RDF triples backed by a hexastore index — six sorted arrays covering every (s, p, o) permutation. This gives O(log n) pattern matching on any combination of bound and unbound positions without needing a full table scan.

title: RDF.Graph
text:
Graph()
Graph(f::Function) An RDF graph backed by a hexastore index for O(log n) pattern matching on any combination of subject, predicate, and object. Supports push!, delete!, in, length, iterate, union, intersect, setdiff, and merge!. The do-block form yields the graph to f and returns it: g = …

length(g)    # number of triples

Concurrency and the term registry
text: RDF.jl interns every distinct term (IRI, literal, blank node) into a global, process-wide registry that maps terms to UInt32 IDs. Two consequences of this design matter for long-running or multi-threaded programs: Threading contract. Interning is thread-safe: any number of threads may build graphs …

title: Set operations
text:
Standard set operations return new graphs without modifying their arguments: g3 = union(g1, g2)      # triples in either g1 or g2
g4 = intersect(g1, g2)  # triples in both g1 and g2
g5 = setdiff(g1, g2)    # triples in g1 but not g2
issubgraph(g1, g2)       # true if every triple in g1 is also in g2

title: Base.merge!
text: merge!(g1::Graph, g2::Graph) -> g1 Merge all triples from g2 into g1 in-place. Blank nodes from g2 that collide with blank nodes already in g1 are renamed to fresh identifiers.

title: RDF.issubgraph
text: issubgraph(g1::Graph, g2::Graph) -> Bool Return true if every triple in g1 also appears in g2.

title: RDF.skolemize
text: skolemize(g::Graph; base::String) -> Graph Return a new graph with all blank nodes replaced by IRIs of the form base * string(id). The base string should end with / or #. skolemize(g; base="http://example.org/.well-known/genid/")

title: RDF.deskolemize
text: deskolemize(g::Graph; base::String) -> Graph Reverse of skolemize: replace IRIs whose value starts with base with fresh blank nodes.

title: Merging and skolemization
text:
merge!(g1, g2)    # add all triples from g2 into g1 (in place)

# Replace blank nodes with IRIs scoped to a base

title: RDF.Triple
text:
Triple(subject, predicate, object) An RDF triple. subject must be a SubjectTerm (IRI, BlankNode, or TripleTerm), predicate must be an IRI, and object may be any ObjectTerm. ex = Namespace("http://example.org/")

title: RDF.GeneralizedTriple
text: GeneralizedTriple(subject, predicate, object) A generalized RDF triple where any position may hold any RDFTerm, including literals in subject/predicate position. Used for non-standard graph formats.

title: RDF.TriplePattern
text: TriplePattern(; subject=nothing, predicate=nothing, object=nothing) A triple pattern for use with match. nothing in any position acts as a wildcard that matches any term.

title: Triples and Quads
text: A Triple holds subject::SubjectTerm, predicate::IRI, object::ObjectTerm. A Quad extends this with graph::GraphName. TriplePattern is used internally by SPARQL — it allows variables (nothing) in any position.

title: Vocabulary API
text: RDF.jl ships built-in constants for the core W3C namespaces (rdf, rdfs, xsd, owl, skos, dc, dcterms, foaf, schema).  For everything else — domain-specific ontologies, frequently-updated vocabularies, or any namespace you want to introspect — Vocabulary and load_vocabulary provide a unified API.

title: RDF Terms
text: RDF data is built from three kinds of terms. All three are subtypes of RDFTerm.

title: RDF.RDFTerm
text: RDFTerm Abstract supertype for all RDF terms: IRI, BlankNode, Literal, and TripleTerm.

title: Type hierarchy
text:
RDFTerm
├── IRI
├── BlankNode
├── Literal
└── TripleTerm   (RDF-star — embedded triples in subject or object position)

title: IRI
text: An absolute IRI (RFC 3987). IRIs identify resources and are used as subjects, predicates, and objects.

title: RDF.IRI
text:
IRI(s::AbstractString) <: RDFTerm An absolute IRI (RFC 3987). Must begin with a scheme (e.g. http:) and contain no unencoded spaces. Use the iri"" string macro for compile-time validation. IRI("http://example.org/Alice")
iri"http://schema.org/Person"

title: RDF.@iri_str
text: iri"http://example.org/foo" String macro that constructs an IRI and validates the value at compile time. Equivalent to IRI(s) but catches invalid IRIs before the program runs.

title: Construction
text:
IRI("http://example.org/Alice")    # runtime validation
iri"http://schema.org/Person"      # compile-time validation Validation rules: must begin with a scheme (http:, urn:, etc.) and must not contain unencoded spaces. IRIs are interned globally — two IRI values with the same string are ===.

title: BlankNode
text: A blank node represents an unnamed resource local to a graph. Blank nodes should be created via blank! to guarantee unique identifiers.

title: RDF.BlankNode

text: ValidationWarning A warning produced by validate, containing: triple::Triple — the offending triplemessage::String — human-readable descriptioncode::Symbol — machine-readable code (:invalid_lang_tag, :ill_typed_literal)

title: Validation
text:
validate checks every literal in a graph against its declared datatype. It returns a vector of ValidationWarning values describing any mismatches. warnings = validate(g)
for w in warnings
    println(w.message, " at ", w.triple)
end

title: Checked datatypes
text: The validator checks lexical forms for the following XSD datatypes: Numeric: xsd:integer, xsd:long, xsd:int, xsd:short, xsd:byte, xsd:nonNegativeInteger, xsd:positiveInteger, xsd:nonPositiveInteger, xsd:negativeInteger, xsd:unsignedLong, xsd:unsignedInt, xsd:unsignedShort, xsd:unsignedByte, …
